recommendation: Keep the no-change audit. Do not re-add the Device.definition-derived clause to Device-type unless the work group reverses FHIR-51500. Any future normalization of Device code search source id/url metadata should be treated as build-source cleanup, because the current rendered search parameter is already Device-code.
issue_request: FHIR-40397 was an Applied/Persuasive OO change request for R6 to align product code search parameters by renaming BiologicallyDerivedProduct product-code to code, making Device product-code search available as code, searching Device code/type across Device.type and DeviceDefinition.classification.type, and removing the duplicate CodeableReference concept branch from Device.definition.
initial_application: Commit 31564391acbf120de82ad6b2720eb87e3270659a changed BiologicallyDerivedProduct product-code to code and changed the Device token parameter code from definition to code. Later FHIR-40397a commits c76ef436f261283b0cc61135e79524a58f6fe506, 115748e7f52b3a98f20d0a3460219cb81e4415e7, and 98dfcfe61357133aa44d5e46a3296d4680c96f16 updated Device.definition/search behavior and added Device relationship guidance. The Jira comment's 934d958cebb69995500fac61b7f24e33d896b217 link is a feature-branch merge, not the substantive Device/BDP application delta.
additional_context: Device, DeviceDefinition, and BiologicallyDerivedProduct are active current-build resources. Later FHIR-51500 intentionally removed Device.definition.resolve().classification.type from Device-type and is already represented on the combined branch by 8b5ae712cb72f13692aab81eebd6d3718407e21e. FHIR-39389/FHIR-42900 canonical-resource work changed DeviceDefinition references toward canonical(DeviceDefinition), and FHIR-40305 was resolved no-change because Device.definition is no longer Codeable.
reconciliation: No source change was made. BiologicallyDerivedProduct-code is present with expression BiologicallyDerivedProduct.productCode; Device-code renders in the current build with Device.type | Device.definition.resolve().classification.type; Device-type is correctly limited to Device.type by FHIR-51500; and Device/DeviceDefinition retain matching device-type binding and narrative guidance.

related_jiras.note: Applied/Persuasive follow-up removed Device.definition.resolve().classification.type from Device-type and already has a combined-branch audit commit.
DeviceDefinition canonical-resource work explains why current Device.definition is canonical(DeviceDefinition), but the issue is broader and not decided here.
Related CanonicalResource decision for DeviceDefinition supports the current canonical-reference context.
Resolved no-change because Device.definition is no longer Codeable, supporting not restoring a CodeableReference concept branch.
No-change ballot issue clarified the Device.definition classification type and Device.type relationship without requiring additional FHIR-40397 edits.
